newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner sees better profits in H2.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner sees better profits in H2.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner ASA said on Tuesday profits were unlikely to improve until the second half of the year.

The shipbuilding, engineering and construction group announced a pre-tax result for the full-year 1996 of 750 million crowns ($112.9 million) compared with 2.44 billion in the corresponding year-ago period.
"The 1996 results are most unsatisfactory," Erik Tonseth, Kvaerner's president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"Cost reductions and restructuring will continue in 1997, but with continuing pressure on margins and short-term overcapacity in some of our businesses, it is unlikely that profits will improve significantly until the second half of 1997," Tonseth said.
